messages.subject: The marginal likelihood of LGCP
parts:
Dear Ina developers, 

Regarding the marginal likelihood output of the LGCP model using inla (i.e., the "mlik" component of INLA output), I have a few questions: 

(1) Is the "mlik" based on the normalized marginal likelihood of the point process? 

(2) Refer equation (3)-(4) of Simpson et al. "Going off grid: LGCP" paper, 

      (2.1) Is the constant C the same in equation (4) and equation (3), C=|Omega|? 
      (2.2) Is the constant C included in "mlik" output or not? 
      (2.3) If I want to compare pi(y|z) with pi(y). I use the definition LGCP definition (equation (1)) to calculate f(y|z) given a fixed z, and use the "mlik" output of inla as the value of f(y).  Shall I adjust "mlik" using a constant?  


Thank you,
 
Hongxiao

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] The marginal likelihood of LGCP
parts:
No, the constant C in (4) is not the same as in (3). In (3) it's |\Omega|, but in (4) it's a combination of \exp(|\Omega|) and the bits of Poisson-probability factors not included in the product.  The first bit is not included in the inla output, but since it's common for p(y|z) and p(y) that is usually not an issue. I believe this is also the case for the other parts, but would need to check the implementation details to be sure.  So in conclusion, I believe you're ok as long as you only look at log likelihood differences for a common domain and common data, but would strongly advise agains assuming that this is the case until you and we have verified this by double checking the implementation details.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] The marginal likelihood of LGCP
parts:
Finn,

Thank you. Can you see if my following reasoning make sense? Since equation (4) is literally a Poisson likelihood, the term in (4) should follow C=\prod_{i=1}^{N+p} alpha_i^{y_i}. After plugging in the faked y and alpha, we get
 
log(C)=\sum_{i=1}^p 0*log(\tilde{alpha}_i) + \sum_{i=1}^N 1*log(0).

I remember from a previous email (by you or someone in your team) that you need to define log(0)=1. If that is the case, then log(C) = N. In the mlik output, if log(C)=N is already included, then pi(y) = mlik - N +|Omega| in order to get back to the LGCP form. If N is not included, then pi(y) = mlik +|Omega|. Correct me if I am wrong.

Hongxiao
